destination.title: Which EFTs admit gravitational UV completion?
destination.question: Which apparently consistent low-energy effective theories admit a UV completion with dynamical gravity, and which proposed necessary conditions help distinguish them?
destination.summary: A shared compatibility question connects foundational discussions and reviews. Definitions, conjectural exclusions and constructive completion are different contributions.

systems: Apparently consistent low-energy EFTs with gravity
regimes: No fixed dimension, compactification or cosmological background
assumptions: A proposed necessary condition is not a sufficient completion criterion
Universality is an intended target, not an established consequence of examples
conventions: String-realizable and generally gravitationally completable classes are not silently identified
Background definitions and humorous summaries are not new classification results
includes: A proposed boundary region as contextual exploration
excludes: An established geometric boundary or complete decision procedure

sourceContributions.qualification: Confirm the c9-to-c10 target change only for the stated completion question. The two candidates, dimension and defining premises remain unspecified; no finer identity or completion result is established. Independent confirmation: u46 explicitly asks about quantum-gravity completion, so its existing c9 specialization can be confirmed at equivalent c10. The row correctly leaves candidate definitions, dimension and premises unspecified; it asserts no completion result or finer identity.

Confirm access through the completion question for low-energy remnants and tests of proposed restrictions. The description does not identify or independently verify the restrictions it calls established. Independent confirmation: u28 addresses low-energy tests of quantum-gravity restrictions, matching the inherited c9 contribution and c10's consistency-testing programme. The row preserves n7's limitation that the restrictions called established are neither identified nor independently verified.

Confirm the infrared-diagnostic contribution at the reused completion destination. Whether quantum gravity guarantees moduli and massless towers remains a separate unresolved target, not an assumed premise. Independent confirmation: The infrared-diagnostic target in u17 addresses completion compatibility at c10 after reuse. The row correctly keeps the separate necessity of moduli and massless towers unresolved rather than importing it as a premise.

Confirm only the completion-boundary role: extending quantitative consistency methods and realizing extremal-functional spectra are distinct unresolved tasks. No physical gravitational completion follows from the suggested spectra. Independent confirmation: Only a boundary role is confirmed. u41 and n9 distinguish extending consistency methods from realizing their suggested spectra in physical gravitational theories, so neither a constructive-completion role nor a new method role at c10 is warranted.

Confirm the broad consistency-review contribution at c10 while retaining the existing c0 application contribution. The review remains multi-target and explicitly offers no guarantee that gravity solves the listed particle-physics problems. Independent confirmation: u37's consistency-review contribution transfers from equivalent c9 to c10 while its separate c0 application contribution remains intact. Both mapped notes preserve the compound programme and explicitly deny guaranteed solutions to the named particle-physics problems.

originalDefinitions.title: Selecting EFTs compatible with quantum gravity
originalDefinitions.question: Which apparently consistent gravitational EFTs admit quantum-gravity completion, and what evidence can distinguish candidate restrictions from established obstructions?
originalDefinitions.summary: A common selection problem accommodates conjectural restrictions, controlled examples and unresolved completion questions. Evidence from known constructions does not classify every possible quantum gravity.

systems: Known string, M-theory and F-theory constructions
targets: Relations among apparently independent EFT parameters
Strength and limitations of proposed consistency evidence
assumptions: Semiclassical consistency and quantum-gravitational completion are separate requirements
conventions: A conjectural criterion, a failure to construct a model and a proved obstruction remain distinct
excludes: Identification of every consistent quantum gravity with the constructions surveyed

sources.title: The String Landscape, the Swampland, and the Missing Corner

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent effective theories can admit a UV completion with dynamical gravity? The lectures formulate this as distinguishing the string landscape from the Swampland.

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent effective field theories admit an ultraviolet completion including quantum gravity? The Swampland denotes those that fail this requirement; the Landscape denotes the string-realizable subset discussed in the review.

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent low-energy effective field theories admit ultraviolet completion into quantum gravity, and what constraints distinguish the Landscape from the Swampland?

sources.title: The Marshland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can the interface between quantum-gravity-compatible theories and incompatible effective theories be identified as a distinct region? The Marshland conjecture names such an interface inside the landscape.

sources.title: The Marshland Conjecture

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent low-energy theories admit a quantum-gravity embedding? The landscape/swampland distinction organizes this embedding question; this paper adopts it as background for a proposed boundary region.

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Which low-energy effective field theories can arise from quantum gravity? The landscape contains theories admitting a gravitational UV completion; the swampland contains those that do not. Proposed necessary conditions can exclude candidates without constructing their UV completions.

sources.title: The Swampland Conjecture Bound Conjecture

evidence.text: Which low-energy effective field theories can admit a consistent ultraviolet completion in quantum gravity? The paper adopts the landscape/swampland terminology as the setting for a different question about the information required to formulate conjectures.

sources.title: Lectures on the string landscape and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which effective field theories can consistently couple to quantum gravity, and how do worldsheet consistency, compactifications, dualities and black holes motivate criteria separating the landscape from the Swampland? These are pedagogical review lectures.

sources.title: The String landscape and the swampland

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent low-energy theories can occur in a consistent quantum theory of gravity? The paper asks whether universal restrictions on string constructions constrain infrared physics despite the large diversity of known vacua.

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for the Effective Field Theories with N Species

evidence.text: How is the gauge weak-gravity cutoff altered when N separated abelian gauge sectors share the same bulk gravity?

sources.title: Populating the swampland: The Case of U(1)**496 and E(8) x U(1)**248

evidence.text: Do U(1)^496 and E8×U(1)^248 ten-dimensional supergravities possess quantum-gravity completions? The paper tests requirements on compactification moduli spaces and on the fate of supersymmetric naked singularities, without assuming a string construction.

sources.title: String Universality in Six Dimensions

evidence.text: Do low-energy consistency conditions characterize the six-dimensional supersymmetric quantum-gravity theories, and does every such consistent theory admit a string compactification? The paper tests this through anomaly constraints, explicit K3 constructions and apparently exceptional infinite families.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Supergravity and String Vacua in Various Dimensions

evidence.text: How strongly does quantum consistency constrain low-energy supersymmetric theories coupled to gravity, and how closely do those constraints match known string constructions in dimensions 10, 8, and 6?

sources.title: An Analysis of Anomaly Cancellation for Theories in D=10

evidence.text: Can the two abelian-containing polynomial candidates be completed into quantum gravity?

sources.title: Weak gravity conjecture and effective field theory

evidence.text: Does satisfying a Weak Gravity Conjecture in a higher-energy gauge theory ensure its validity after Higgsing, and what weaker constraint on gauge EFTs might survive when conventional WGC bounds fail?

sources.title: An infinite swampland of U(1) charge spectra in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which massless charge spectra of six-dimensional N = 1 supergravity with one gauged U(1) satisfy known consistency tests, and which can arise in F-theory?

sources.title: An infinite swampland of U(1) charge spectra in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Do anomaly cancellation and other known consistency conditions bound the massless charge spectra of 6D supergravity with one U(1), and how do these spectra compare with F-theory realizations and Higgsed nonabelian theories?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: How does a P^2 hybrid base change characteristic widths and logarithmic distance scales relative to P^1 hybrids?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: How far can scalar fields move in an unstabilized Calabi–Yau vector-multiplet moduli space before its effective description changes substantially?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Does the finite-width and logarithmic-distance pattern persist in a second two-parameter model with P^1 and orbifold hybrids?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Do characteristic non-geometric excursions and logarithmic distance scales remain of order the Planck scale in the studied Calabi–Yau moduli spaces?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Can many small non-geometric regions combine into a parametrically large pre-asymptotic geodesic excursion as moduli count increases?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Can characteristic LG excursions remain small when many moduli are available, and what can a symmetry-restricted calculation establish?

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Can a finite non-geometric phase provide a large proper displacement before the exponential mass decrease associated with large volume becomes relevant? The paper follows trajectories from such phases toward infinite-distance regions.

sources.title: The Refined Swampland Distance Conjecture in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: How do proper distances behave across geometric, LG, and hybrid regimes in a two-complex-dimensional Calabi–Yau moduli space?

sources.title: De Sitter Space and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a quantum-gravity scalar potential have an arbitrarily small positive-energy slope?

sources.title: de Sitter Extrema and the Swampland

evidence.text: Could a restriction involving both slope and curvature accommodate unstable classical extrema while still constraining positive-potential scalar theories?

sources.title: Theta-problem and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Which gauge couplings and theta angles of an infrared photon coupled to gravity admit a consistent ultraviolet completion?

sources.title: Theta-problem and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a quantum-gravity completion permit continuously adjustable couplings that are independent of scalar expectation values?

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Which conjectured quantum-gravity constraints can be tested by a controlled compactification limit with a weak gauge interaction and finite gravitational coupling?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for the Effective Field Theories with N Species

evidence.text: Divide S < EL by E and insert the relativistic gas ratio S/E. This produces the lower size bound needed to test compatibility with the independently derived collapse upper bound.

sources.title: Populating the swampland: The Case of U(1)**496 and E(8) x U(1)**248

evidence.text: Shift the seed's asymptotic radius above one, rotate its charge into a ten-dimensional gauge U(1), and rescale the final internal modulus. This isolates a finite Wilson-line-zero locus outside the repulson without relying on geometric self-duality there.

sources.title: String Universality in Six Dimensions

evidence.text: Use group trace identities to remove irreducible tr F^4 anomalies, then solve Green–Schwarz factorization of the remaining polynomial. For the worked model the irreducible constraints are M−BN=8 and 2N−A(N−8)−BM=0.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Supergravity and String Vacua in Various Dimensions

evidence.text: Green–Schwarz anomaly cancellation uses factorization of anomaly polynomials and exchange of two-form fields. In 6D, I8 = ½ Ωαβ X4α X4β with Ω of signature (1,T). Legible constraints include H−V = 273−29T, a·a = 9−T, and proper-sign gauge kinetic terms requiring j·bi > 0.

sources.title: An Analysis of Anomaly Cancellation for Theories in D=10

evidence.text: List allowed factor terms, expand their product, solve coefficients fixed by distinctive monomials and test the residual equations. A contradiction identifies the curvature terms carrying the obstruction.

sources.title: Weak gravity conjecture and effective field theory

evidence.text: Track gauge-boson mass eigenstates and the surviving charge lattice after Higgsing, then iterate the construction through a chain of Abelian gauge groups.

sources.title: Swampland Revisited

evidence.text: How should swampland conjectures distinguish effective theories admitting ultraviolet quantum-gravity completion, and how justified is excluding de Sitter vacua given cosmological observations and disputed string constructions?

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: Which proposed restrictions distinguish scalar effective theories admitting quantum-gravity completion from theories in the swampland?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: How can quantum gravity constrain an effective theory below its apparent cutoff? A Swampland scale indicates when modification becomes necessary for eventual completion, even when no immediate inconsistency occurs at that energy.

sources.title: Lectures in quantum gravity

evidence.text: What low-energy framework and consistency tests should quantum-gravity UV completions recover, and what can semiclassical black holes teach before a full completion is known?

sources.title: The anomaly that was not meant IIB

evidence.text: Do the alternative anomaly-free realizations admit quantum-gravity completions, or do further consistency conditions place them in the Swampland?

sources.title: An infinite swampland of U(1) charge spectra in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Construct a suitable nonabelian model, use two adjoints to break to U(1), and read the daughter charge spectrum. The source supplies an existence outline, while leaving the explicit abelian geometry and charge branching unshown.

sources.title: The String Landscape, the Swampland, and the Missing Corner

evidence.text: Use holomorphic-map localization and a genus/degree organization for the A-model, or mirror-period methods for genus-zero B-model data. The packet supplies the framework rather than a computed partition function.

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Allocate excitation among factors in proportion to their positive indices, then control integer rounding. For Jacobi products this yields a candidate large-level charge, whose survival still requires a nonzero final coefficient.

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Evaluate proposed constraints against controlled constructions and independently motivated infrared arguments, recording assumptions and construction quality. The review distinguishes complete worldsheet constructions from more assumption-dependent string-inspired models and treats their agreement as graded evidence.

sources.title: The Marshland Conjecture

evidence.text: The source identifies entanglement entropy of massless-field vacuum fluctuations as the basis of the imported calculation. It does not supply an entropy functional, regulator, gravitational entropy comparison, or intermediate steps from which that calculation could be reproduced.

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Infer candidate necessary conditions from semiclassical black-hole arguments and string examples, then test further examples, mutual consistency, and phenomenological consequences. Revise proposals when low-energy potentials or observations expose obstructions or loopholes.

destinations.title: Can the two abelian-containing polynomial candidates be completed into quantum gravity?
Which apparently consistent effective theories can admit a UV completion with dynamical gravity? The lectures formulate this as distinguishing the string landscape from the Swampland.
Which conjectured quantum-gravity constraints can be tested by a controlled compactification limit with a weak gauge interaction and finite gravitational coupling?

Which apparently consistent effective field theories admit an ultraviolet completion including quantum gravity? The Swampland denotes those that fail this requirement; the Landscape denotes the string-realizable subset discussed in the review.
Which apparently consistent low-energy effective field theories admit ultraviolet completion into quantum gravity, and what constraints distinguish the Landscape from the Swampland?

Can the interface between quantum-gravity-compatible theories and incompatible effective theories be identified as a distinct region? The Marshland conjecture names such an interface inside the landscape.

Which apparently consistent low-energy theories admit a quantum-gravity embedding? The landscape/swampland distinction organizes this embedding question; this paper adopts it as background for a proposed boundary region.

Which low-energy effective field theories can arise from quantum gravity? The landscape contains theories admitting a gravitational UV completion; the swampland contains those that do not. Proposed necessary conditions can exclude candidates without constructing their UV completions.
Could quantum-gravity consistency require charged sources that also modify the compactification obstruction?

Can a quantum-gravity bound expose artificial removal of a source that should drive spacetime evolution? The proposed test follows charged objects away from a supersymmetric vacuum while examining the modified background equations.

Can the large-D limit of an apparently consistent gravity effective theory belong to quantum gravity? The paper asks whether known conjectures remain restrictive and whether dimension-dependent tower masses suggest additional restrictions.

Which low-energy effective field theories can admit a consistent ultraviolet completion in quantum gravity? The paper adopts the landscape/swampland terminology as the setting for a different question about the information required to formulate conjectures.

Which effective field theories can consistently couple to quantum gravity, and how do worldsheet consistency, compactifications, dualities and black holes motivate criteria separating the landscape from the Swampland? These are pedagogical review lectures.

Which apparently consistent low-energy theories can occur in a consistent quantum theory of gravity? The paper asks whether universal restrictions on string constructions constrain infrared physics despite the large diversity of known vacua.

sources.title: Is String Phenomenology an Oxymoron?

evidence.text: Literature-based assessment using the relation between QFT and particular models as an analogy for string theory and its scenarios. The essay separates generic statements, construction-dependent predictions and observational challenges rather than presenting a new derivation.

sources.title: TF1 Snowmass Report: Quantum gravity, string theory, and black holes

evidence.text: Cosmological perturbation theory computes correlation functions and possible non-Gaussian signatures of additional inflationary fields. These calculations are related to scattering-amplitude questions in de Sitter, flat, and AdS spacetimes.

sources.title: Snowmass Theory Frontier Report

evidence.text: Amplitude techniques include recursive tree constructions, unitarity-based construction of loop amplitudes, geometric representations, and color–kinematics duality. The double copy constructs gravitational amplitudes by replacing gauge-theory color factors with kinematic factors.

sources.title: Formal theory: status and outlook

evidence.text: The reviewed island method uses generalized entropy S_gen = [k c^3/(4Gℏ)] A(X) + S_bulk, with X a quantum extremal surface and S_bulk the entropy of a region bounded by X. The overview instructs taking an extremal value; k denotes Boltzmann's constant.

sources.title: Formal theory at ICHEP 2024

evidence.text: Reviewed amplitude tools include recursion relations and the amplituhedron in idealized supersymmetric settings, plus color-kinematics duality and double copy connecting gauge-theory and gravitational scattering. Their role is to provide structural insights relevant to difficult precision calculations.

sources.title: Is String Phenomenology an Oxymoron?

evidence.text: Reviewed tools include dimensional reduction, effective field theory, geometry, branes, quantized fluxes, perturbative corrections and nonperturbative superpotentials. Phenomenological comparisons concern superparticle spectra, inflationary observables and post-inflationary cosmology.
